paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God's love doesn't quit when His people walk away. He loved Israel as a child, taught Ephraim to walk and bent down to feed them (Hosea 11:1, 3, 4). And what did they do? "The more I called Israel, the farther they departed from Me" (Hosea 11:2). If that was my kid, I'd be loud AND dramatic about it, but look at what the LORD does next.

The warnings are real, friend. He says a sword will flash through their cities, because they refused to repent (Hosea 11:5, 6). Then comes the turn: "How could I give you up, O Ephraim?" and "My heart is turned within Me; My compassion is stirred!" (Hosea 11:8). Why won't He pour out His anger? "For I am God and not man—the Holy One among you—and I will not come in wrath" (Hosea 11:9). His mercy doesn't depend on how well we did. It rests on who HE is.

So here's why this matters to you, baker. You will drift sometimes, and so will I. But the LORD is the One who calls, and He promises to bring His children home: "Then I will settle them in their homes, declares the LORD" (Hosea 11:11). Don't hide from a God like that. Walk back toward Him, because He has never stopped calling you.
